newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOV'T APPROVES $3.9 MILLION L. ENERGY LOAN.
newsitem.headline: GOV'T APPROVES $3.9 MILLION L. ENERGY LOAN.

text.p: The Lithuanian government decided to give a $3.9 million credit to Lithuanian Energy to buy heating oil.
The government's press office said in a statement that the $3.9 million will be taken from an earlier J.P. Morgan syndicated credit and will be used to buy heating oil.
"Lithuanian Energy will be given a $3.9 million credit from the J.P. Morgan syndicated loan taken in the name of the state to buy heating oil in July," the statement said.
The statement also said that the loan matures on May 1, 1998 and the interest is one percent higher than the state borrowed at.
The government also said that the heating oil should be acquired through a tender and the amount to be bought is up to 60,000 tonnes.
